blogs.title: From Blocky to Butterfly: How a Classic Algorithm is Revolutionizing AI Fine-Tuning
blogs.description: Explore how researchers are borrowing a mathematical structure from the 1960s Fast Fourier Transform—the 'butterfly' graph—to solve a modern AI problem. This post explains how the new 'Orthogonal Butterfly' (BOFT) method replaces rigid, block-diagonal matrices with flexible, sparse structures, allowing large models to adapt to new tasks with significantly fewer parameters while maintaining high performance.

blogs.title: The Information Highway: Visualizing How AI Models Learn Without Forgetting
blogs.description: Dive into the fascinating 'information transmission' framework used in the latest parameter-efficient fine-tuning research. We break down how scientists are treating neural network weight updates like data flowing through a network grid, ensuring that every piece of pre-trained knowledge is preserved (via orthogonal transformations) while efficiently transmitting new task-specific information.

blogs.title: BOFT vs. LoRA: The New Contender for Efficient Large Model Adaptation
blogs.description: Everyone knows LoRA, but is there a better way? This post compares the popular low-rank adaptation method with the emerging Orthogonal Butterfly (BOFT) technique. We analyze why preserving the geometric angles between neurons (orthogonality) might offer better stability and generalization than adding low-rank matrices, and how BOFT achieves this with a fraction of the computational cost of previous orthogonal methods.

blogs.title: One Method to Rule Them All: Fine-Tuning Text, Images, and Diffusion Models with BOFT
blogs.description: Discover why Orthogonal Butterfly (BOFT) is being hailed as a universal solution for adapting foundation models. From Large Language Models to Stable Diffusion and Vision Transformers, this post highlights extensive empirical results showing how BOFT outperforms state-of-the-art methods across diverse domains by balancing expressivity and regularity through its unique structured matrix design.
